title: Cuando and mientras: events in the past

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *cuando* with the *indefinido* from A2 Unit 13: it joins one finished event to the moment when another happened. You also know *mientras* for two actions that go on at the same time, and the *indefinido* and the *imperfecto* from A2 Units 11 and 21. The history of the interventions mixes both: one event, and something else going on meanwhile.

sections.title: Two connectors
rows: one event, then another: *Cuando terminó la guerra, España entregó Puerto Rico.*
two actions at the same time: *Mientras se construía el canal, llegaron trabajadores.*

items.spanish: Cuando terminó la guerra, España entregó Puerto Rico a Estados Unidos.
items.english: When the war ended, Spain handed Puerto Rico over to the United States.

items.spanish: Mientras Cuba luchaba por su independencia, Estados Unidos entró en el conflicto.
items.english: While Cuba was fighting for its independence, the United States entered the conflict.

items.spanish: Mientras se construía el canal, llegaron a Panamá muchos trabajadores.
items.english: While the canal was being built, many workers arrived in Panama.

items.spanish: Cuando los marines salieron de Nicaragua en 1933, terminó la guerrilla de Sandino.
items.english: When the marines left Nicaragua in 1933, Sandino's guerrilla war came to an end.

sections.content: *Cuando* + *indefinido* often gives the starting point or result of a main event; *mientras* + *imperfecto* gives the background that was going on. With *cuando* at the start of the sentence, put a comma after its clause.
